doc.title: 68088_Wilbur B. Ware, Sr oral history interview

chapter: Drugs and the House of Correction
title: His first whiskey in Quincy as a teenager
summary: He drinks a pitcher of whiskey at fifteen in Quincy and is violently sick.

story.theme_name: Drink, drugs and the bandstand's casualties
story.community_name: Drugs and drink on the bandstand and the road

blocks.x: Same thing. When I first went to Quincy, Illinois, with the band -- not Flip's band, but this other band, Roy, I hadn't -- I mean, I would drink a little wine with the gang, because there were 10 of us on one pint, you know, and we'd swear we were high. But when I got to Quincy, they were serving it in these little pitchers -- whiskey -- and I didn't know nothing about drinking whiskey;

I was just sipping wine. So when we got upstairs, one of the guys says, "Do you drink?" "Yeah" -- I mean, I'm trying to be a man, and I wasn't but 15. "Okay, here, take a drink." And it was this little small pitcher; and he was pouring me a shot -- I picked up the pitcher and drank the whole pitcher.

He looked at me ... and I'm thinking I'd done something big -- I'm grown, you know? He said, "I bet you won't do that again." And I ... he said, "I'll buy a load." -- I think it cost something like 50¢ or 35¢, something like that -- and I threw that down.

And he looked at me ... but he didn't tell me, see, you weren't supposed to drink like that. But he said, "You gonna learn it" -- and actually, I did. I got up from the table; we were getting ready to go. The last thing I remember when I opened that door to go, and the next thing I knew, I fell right flat on my face. And naturally I was sick, oh, all that morning, and I'm sick and cold and all, and I'm just getting down and gagging.

But did you think that stopped me? No. I had to play it straight out. I didn't think nothing was smart about it; I didn't look at it like that. As far as the dope was concerned, I just didn't want to get sick. I didn't really enjoy what they called the high, because I didn't know -- I was asleep.
